gaps: AWaRe groups taken only from the WHO 2025 workbook (B09489). The 2025 workbook carries no ATC codes for 'Not recommended' combinations, so atc is empty for those.
WHO classifies two products as 'not assigned' ATC (cefoselis, micronomicin); atc left empty.

WHO classes some antibiotics by route (colistin, fosfomycin, kanamycin, metronidazole, minocycline, neomycin, ornidazole, polymyxin B, rifamycin, streptomycin, tinidazole, vancomycin); MedSync must map by route as well as INN. Fosfomycin and minocycline change group with route (IV Reserve, oral Watch).

AWaRe covers systemic antibacterials (mainly ATC J01, with some A07 and P01 entries). Ophthalmic, otic and topical products on EMHSLU 2023 (chloramphenicol, ciprofloxacin, gentamicin, tetracycline, tobramycin, oxytetracycline + polymyxin B, neomycin, framycetin, silver sulphadiazine, metronidazole gel) need a signed rule on whether they are counted; the candidate default is to exclude them from AWaRe shares.
TB and leprosy medicines are not in the AWaRe workbook except rifamycins and some fluoroquinolones and linezolid. Signers must decide whether programme TB use counts in hospital AWaRe shares.

Products on the Ugandan market were not verified against the National Drug Authority register: nda.or.ug could not be reached from this environment. The list is therefore the full WHO 2025 list, with EMHSLU 2023 presence marked; 'plausibly on the Ugandan market' is not asserted beyond EMHSLU and the Uganda PPS.
EMHSLU 2023 presence read from the full PDF text of the guluhospital.net copy; the MoH library copy could not be opened. sulfadiazine is marked unknown because its entry on p35 was not read.
The EMHSLU 2023 amoxicillin + clavulanic acid COPD entry is printed as '600mg+25mg'; likely a typographical error, to be verified by the pharmacist reviewer.
The 2025 Expert Committee report (B09544) describing which antibiotics were added or reclassified in 2025 could not be opened, so changes from 2023 are not listed.
WHO DDD values (ATC/DDD index) were not collected; any DDD metric needs them.
